verdict.rationale: Svelte's own GitHub description says it is a compiler that turns declarative components into efficient JavaScript that surgically updates the DOM. Its docs confirm the compiler emits lean, optimized JavaScript, and developers update state as plain variables with no diffing API. Community reports corroborate readable compiled output and performance gains after migrating from React; missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation or benchmarks explaining the compiled DOM-update mechanism, and one community report notes Svelte 4 rendering slows at very high element counts.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on a compiler to translate my components into efficient, surgical DOM updates instead of writing manual diffing code

citations.quote: It's a compiler that takes your declarative components and converts them into efficient JavaScript that surgically updates the DOM.
It uses a compiler to turn declarative components written in HTML, CSS and JavaScript...into lean, tightly optimized JavaScript.
there is no API for interacting with state — `count` is just a number, rather than an object or a function, and you can update it like you would update any other variable.
The generated code is readable: they stepped through compiled component code while profiling a layout-per-frame issue and traced it to their own function.
